question: In early 2024, the Agency for State Financial Information Technology in France awarded the contract for ‘PLACE’, a platform that manages government procurement, to a US firm1. The contract was awarded directly, i.e.

without a call for tenders, to a company from outside the EU, which will now be able to access sensitive information on the 300 000 or so companies responding to calls for tenders from all French administrations, including those in charge of the army, foreign affairs and the health service.
This decision is all the more incomprehensible as a French SME that created and developed PLACE was excluded from managing the application. 1.
As part of the fight against commercial and industrial espionage, is the Commission monitoring the award of strategic contracts to companies from outside the EU?
Has the PLACE platform received EU funding for its development?
Will the Commission reflect, if necessary, on ways to ensure that software developed by EU funds remains administered by European companies?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (13.6.2025) Since 12 July 2023, the Foreign Subsidies Regulation (FSR)1 enables the Commission to address the distortive effect on competition of foreign subsidies.

In particular, it introduced a notification obligation for bidders in public procurement procedures falling within the scope of application of the Regulation with an estimated value equal or greater than EUR 250 million.

In so far as the Commission’s own funding activities are concerned, the recast of the Financial Regulation2 has introduced a horizontal legal basis in its Article 136 in order to identify sensitive award procedures, e.g. concerning strategic assets and interests such as satellite infrastructure.

This allows for the introduction of participation restrictions, including for third country ownership and control of applicants and tenderers, where necessary, to protect security and public order of the EU and its Member States.

Furthermore, with the Single Market Strategy3 presented on 21 May 2025, the Commission has reaffirmed its commitment to review the EU public procurement framework in 2026 also with a view to introducing European preference criteria in EU public procurement for certain strategic technologies and sectors, while ensuring the competitiveness of tenders.
The development of the platform as referred to by the Honourable Member has not been supported with EU funds.
